hints: For a longest strictly increasing subsequence, equal values cannot extend one another.
Maintain tails[length] as the smallest possible ending value of an increasing subsequence of that length.
Binary-search the first tail greater than or equal to the new value and replace it.
analogy: Keep the easiest-to-extend ending value for every subsequence length.
example: For 3,1,2,5,4, tails evolve to [1,2,4], so the longest length is 3.
algorithm: For each x, lower_bound tails for x; replace that entry, or append if x exceeds every tail. The number of tails is the answer.
correctness: For each length, a smaller tail is at least as useful as a larger one for future extensions; replacing maintains the best representative and preserves the maximum attainable length.
complexity: O(n log n) time and O(n) space.
